extracted.intended_audience: creative writers (especially those using regional/dialect speech and Americanisms)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using regional dialect, Americanisms, and rustic idiom in literary writing (dialogue, pastoral, and poetic pieces), balancing authenticity, style, and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticate supposed Americanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not assume a colloquialism is a recent American invention; many words and phrases thought to be 'Americanisms' occur in older English texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research historical usage in dictionaries and older sources (Chaucer, Gower, Jonson, Middleton, Beaumont and Fletcher, Skelton, Hakluyt, etc.) before labeling a usage as novel. The author shows multiple examples (e.g., 'at onst', 'to progress', 'cursedness/cuss', 'green sauce', 'let the world slide') demonstrating that apparent neologisms often have long antecedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve a natural/native voice (be 'naïf')
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to be natural and native to your age/place: 'be natural, of being naïf, which means nothing more than native, of belonging to the age and country in which you are born.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid contrived pseudo-classicality or affected mannerisms; favor a straightforward, native-sounding voice appropriate to the characters and setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dialectal elements as poetic/ stylistic advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: Short syllables, abbreviations, contractions, and novel rhymes in local speech can be strengths for poetry and stylistic freshness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage elements like 'several short, light syllables, abbreviations, contractiones, many short, light syllables, new rhymes' (Goethe on Hebel) to create a style well suited to regional or pastoral verse — compress these elements into 'happy constructions and vivid forms' to form an effective style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid purism without linguistic/historical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the attitude of speech‑purists who censor dialects without understanding their history and affinities: 'a hearty contempt for the speech-gilders who affect purism without any thorough... knowledge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude or edit out dialectal usages merely on aesthetic prejudice; understand origins and functions before deeming them incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance humor's exuberance with wit's precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that 'the tendency of humor is always towards overplus of expression, while the very essence of wit is its logical precision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using comic or exaggerated dialectal speech, keep a counterbalance of precision so the writing remains clear and doesn't descend into meaningless excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and study erratic words and phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect odd or local words and phrases encountered in speech or reading; they 'may throw light on the meaning of other words, on the relationship of languages, or even on history itself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain notes of dialectal lexicon (vocabulary, proverbs, idioms) as resources for texture, etymology, characterization, and historical resonance; many concrete examples are provided throughout the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render pronunciation and intonation precisely in dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey subtle variants of pronunciation and intonation (e.g., the multiple 'well' forms) to capture authentic speech patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use phonetic spellings and variant forms to show differences of tone, length, nasal quality, aspiration, and truncation (examples: 'wul', 'ooa-ahl', 'wahl', ''l I dunno', 'wal'); be attentive to how small changes convey deliberation, impatience, or resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mere imitation of earlier provincial dialects
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attempt to be merely what an earlier provincial dialect already was; imitation risks making the work 'a bore.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for an authentic contemporary voice grounded in place and time rather than reproducing a historical provincial manner for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit dialectal register to context and genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the degree of dialect and the level of sentiment to the piece: dialect can admit 'more sentiment and a higher tone' in pastoral or poetic contexts without incongruity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust dialectal intensity for the form (e.g., pastoral verse vs. comic sketch) so that sentiment and elevated language sit naturally with colloquial speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local idioms and proverbs judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Local proverbs and sayings add flavor, but many are 'too long-skirted' or coarse and lack character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concise, characterful sayings that feel native ('Mean enough to steal acorns from a blind hog', 'Quicker 'n greased lightnin'') and avoid overlong or bluntly coarse proverbs that do not serve the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dialect to dramatize and create vivid imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional speech and exaggeration can convert a dry fact into vivid, comic, or poetic image (e.g., 'a lump of quicksilver in each boot').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ figurative exaggeration and local turns of phrase to make descriptions lively and memorable; dialectal wording often yields striking conceits and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the 'jus et norma loquendi' — expressive freedom within stylistic norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold classical rules of tasteful speech while allowing liberty: the author references Horace and Galiani's definition of sublime oratory — 'l'art de tout dire sans être mis à la Bastille...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to say what must be said without breaching the broader norms of propriety or intelligibility; be bold but avoid gratuitous offense or incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use etymological/ comparative insight to inform choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore affinities across languages and history (Latin, Old English, French, Icelandic, German, Italian) to explain or justify regional usages and senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing an odd or archaic term, consider and, if helpful, hint at its linguistic relatives or history (e.g., 'chist' ~ cista; 'cotton' ~ A.S. cvead/Icelandic qvoda) to deepen authenticity and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overuse or caricature of dialect
rubrics_metrics.description: While dialect is valuable, overuse or crude caricature can reduce readability and artistic merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ dialect selectively and purposefully for character, humor, or tone; avoid rendering every utterance in heavy phonetic spelling or exaggerated orthography that distracts or bores the reader.
